newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian blue chips notch gains in run-up to budget.
newsitem.headline: Indian blue chips notch gains in run-up to budget.

text.p: ** (1200 GMT) - Shares end sharply higher as countdown
begins to Friday's budget
** Bombay's benchmark index jumps 62.90 pts, or 1.87 pct,
to 3,427.87, breaks out of lacklustre trade
** Creeping market optimism ahead of Friday's 1997/98
budget (April-March) pushes up stock prices
** Last day of end-account-trade at Bombay bourse leads to
renewed speculative activity, say traders
** National exchange index rises 2.47 pct to 992.75 points
** Madras share index gains 50.60 points to 3,393.80 and
Calcutta index 5.74 pts to 448.45
Blue chips at major Indian bourses rallied in hectic trade on Thursday on market optimism ahead of Friday's budget, dealers said.
Position squaring by speculators on the last day of the weekly account at the BSE also drove up prices, they said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presents his second budget to Parliament on Friday at 5.00 p.m (1130 GMT).
"The levels of expectation are very low. There is a very small downward risk at this stage," said chief dealer Sanjay Vaid at Bombay-based Lloyds Securities.

The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark index jumped 62.90 points, or 1.87 percent to end at 3,427.87, above the intra-day low of 3,379.10. The index surge came after lacklustre and dull trading seen in the last few days.
Some analysts said rising market optimism that the government would announce strong steps in the budget to revive a slowing economy and boost markets stoked thursday's rally.
"My expectation from the budget is not of policy announcements, it's more of implementation," Subra Subramanian, India research director at foreign securities firm H.G. Asia told Reuters.

Traders said they were looking for a removal of double taxation on company dividends and the freedom for firms to buy back their own shares in the budget. They were also hoping for a reduction in a 7.5 percent corporate surcharge and a revamped minimum alternate tax.
"The real focus should be on rebuilding confidence among Indian industrialists and the investing public," said Tushar Sarda, president and chief executive officer at CRB-Daewoo Securities Ltd.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
